text: The temperature of the reaction mixture rises as energy is given out.
The transport system made up of the heart, blood vessels, and blood that circulates nutrients, gases, and wastes throughout the body.
Bony enclosures and shock-absorbing fluid protect the delicate tissues of the central nervous system.
A visual impairment where close objects are seen clearly but distant ones look blurry, corrected using a diverging lens whose focal length equals the person's far point, taken as a negative value.
To correct myopia, the focal length of the concave lens must equal the negative of the person's far point.
A rule that gives the direction of the magnetic field around a current-carrying conductor.
A principle stating that only about ten percent of the food energy available at one trophic level is transferred and incorporated into the body of the next trophic level.
Classification of algal reproduction by the relative size and motility of the fusing gametes.
The relative positions of the calyx, corolla, and androecium with respect to the ovary on the thalamus, deciding whether the ovary is superior, half-inferior, or inferior.
The numerical ratio of the volume of carbon dioxide given out to the volume of oxygen taken in during respiration.
A classification system in which elements with similar properties are grouped in threes, the atomic weight of the middle element being close to the mean of the weights of the other two.
In a triad, the atomic weight of the middle element is close to the mean of the atomic weights of the first and third elements.
Constructing temporary names and three-letter symbols directly from the digits of the atomic number.
The energy needed to remove one mole of electrons completely from one mole of isolated gaseous hydrogen atoms in their ground state.
The way the energy needed to remove an electron from a gaseous atom changes through the periodic table: it generally grows across a period and falls down a group.
A measure of the stability and strength of an ionic crystal lattice.
The sum of the covalent radii of the two bonded atoms.
Cleaving the C=C bond and capping the two fragments with carbonyl oxygens shows where the original double bond sat and how the carbon chain was branched.
The ratio of the length of a circular arc to the radius of that circle, giving the angular span in a plane.
The total area of the six square faces of a cube, found as six times the square of its side length.
The ratio of the linear size of an image to the linear size of the object; for areas, the magnification is the square of this value.
Displacement is the sum of the distance covered at the initial speed and the extra distance contributed by the acceleration.
Stopping distance grows with the square of the initial velocity.
Continuously redirecting the velocity vector toward the circle's centre produces radial acceleration.
The dot product of two vectors is a scalar: the product of their magnitudes multiplied further by the cosine of the angle between their directions.
The total pressure at a given depth in a liquid at rest equals the atmospheric pressure on the surface plus the pressure due to the weight of the liquid column above that depth.
The ratio of the shearing stress applied to a fluid layer to the resulting velocity gradient (strain rate) across the layers.
The ratio of the surface force on a boundary line of a liquid film to twice the length of that line; the factor two accounts for the film's two surfaces.
Mitotic division of the generative cell inside a pollen grain, producing two non-motile male gametes for double fertilisation.
The charges on the metal ion and all ligands add up to the overall charge of the coordination entity.
The configuration of d4 to d7 ions hangs on the relative sizes of the crystal-field splitting energy (delta_o) and the pairing energy (P).
Classification of halogenated organic compounds by the number of halogen atoms present and by the hybridisation of the carbon atom that carries the halogen.
Alcohols and phenols are classified by the number of hydroxyl groups and by how substituted the carbon bearing the -OH group is.
In Markovnikov addition, the hydroxyl group attaches to the more substituted carbon of the double bond.
Phenols are acidic because the phenoxide ion they form is stabilised when the negative charge spreads over the benzene ring.
Low temperature is critical because aryl diazonium salts decompose when warm.
Replacing the diazonium group of an aryl diazonium salt by Cl, Br, or CN using copper(I) salts (Sandmeyer-type reactions).
The potential of a point charge falls off as 1/r with distance and keeps the algebraic sign of the charge.
The total electrostatic potential at a point due to a collection of point charges is the algebraic sum of the potentials produced by each charge individually.
Capacitance depends only on the geometry of the conducting plates and the permittivity of the medium between them.
The radius of the circular orbit traced by a charged particle moving perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field.
The orbital frequency depends on neither the particle's speed nor the orbit radius.
The magnetic field grows with current and element length, and falls with the square of the distance.
The inductance of a solenoid varies with the square of the number of turns per unit length.
The tangent of the phase difference equals the ratio of net reactance to resistance, showing whether current leads or lags the voltage.
The fraction of real power transferred to an alternating current circuit relative to the apparent volt-ampere product, given by the cosine of the phase difference (power factor).
Only the resistive part of an AC circuit dissipates energy, so the average power involves the cosine of the phase angle.
Tiny finger-like projections on the inner wall of the small intestine that enlarge the absorbing surface and help nutrients pass into the blood.
When equal masses of the same substance at different temperatures are mixed, the final temperature lies at the mean of the two initial temperatures, assuming no heat is lost to the surroundings.
The mixture's final temperature is the average of the two initial temperatures.
Distance is the speed of the object multiplied by the time it travels.
A fluid presses on the bottom and the walls of its container, and this pressure grows with the depth of the liquid column.
The pressure exerted by the weight of the air column in the atmosphere acting on a unit area.
Loudness tracks the intensity of a sound: it grows with the square of the vibration amplitude and is expressed in decibels (dB).
Total magnification is the magnifying power of the eyepiece multiplied by that of the objective lens.
The ratio of the net change in position (displacement) of an object to the total time taken for that change.
The mechanical advantage of a ramp equals the length of the incline divided by its vertical height.
The ratio of the effort arm length to the load arm length, which tells how much force a lever multiplies.
The sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms in one molecule of a covalent compound, expressed in unified atomic mass units (u).
The sum of the atomic masses of all the atoms in the simplest formula unit of an ionic compound.
Albedo is a measure of how reflective a surface is: the fraction of incoming solar radiation it bounces back to space.
Uneven heating across the globe creates pressure belts, while the Earth's rotation turns winds rightward in the Northern Hemisphere and leftward in the Southern Hemisphere.
